verses.zh: 众海岛啊，当听我言！远方的众民哪，留心而听！自我出胎，耶和华就选召我；自出母腹，他就提我的名。
verses.en: Listen to me, you coastlands![NOTE:1] Pay attention, you people who live far away!The Lord summoned me from birth;[NOTE:2] he commissioned me when my mother brought me into the world.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “islands” (NASB, NIV); NLT “in far-off lands.”sn The Lord’s special servant, introduced in chap. 42, speaks here of his commission.
Heb “called me from the womb.”
Heb “from the inner parts of my mother he mentioned my name.”
verses.commentary:
49:1 "Listen" See full note on the introductory IMPERATIVE at Isa. 48:1.

There are two IMPERATIVES that introduce this new literary unit.

- listen ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570)

- pay attention ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 904, KB 1151)

God's revelation of Himself and His purposes was meant to be heard, understood, and acted on!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (Shema)

▣ "O islands. . .peoples from afar" These parallel phrases show the universal
implications of the "servant's" task (cf. Isa. 42:6-7). The love of God

- remembers its covenant with Abraham's descendants (cf. Isa. 49:5-6b)

- remembers the promise to all humans, Gen. 3:15; 12:3 (cf. Isa. 49:6c; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDMPTIVE PLAN)

There is a dual aspect to YHWH's message

- to the returning covenant people from exile by Cyrus' decree

- to the returning nations under the Servant/Messiah

There is always in Isaiah an eye on the present (Assyria); the near Future
(Neo-Babylon, Persia), and the distant future (gospel age). YHWH's desires for Israel's

- righteousness

- revelation to the nations

was never fulfilled. The evangelistic mandate (see note at Isa. 40:15)
was transferred to the NT people of God (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT PREDICTIONS OF THE FUTURE vs. NT PREDICTIONS

▣ "The Lord called Me from the womb" The NASB has the
PRONOUNS capitalized to show that they think they refer to the Messiah, the individualized Servant
(i.e. LXX of Isa. 52:14). God's special call is expressed in the Servant's prenatal call (cf. v. 5, as was Jeremiah, cf. Jer. 1:5). There is an
obvious tension in these "Servant" passages between the individual and corporate aspects of the Servant.
It is clear from Isa. 41:8-9; 42:19; 43:10; 49:3 that the title is used for corporate Israel. However, the individual focus of the
SINGULAR PRONOUNS of chapter 49 and the work of the individual in Isa. 52:13-53:12
show that these passages have a dual focus. This dual focus can also be seen in chapter 42. Verses 1-4
relate to the Messiah, while Isa. 49:19-21 are obviously corporate Israel. Israel was called to be a kingdom
of priests to bring the world to God, Gen. 12:1-3; Exod. 19:4-6. She failed because she did not and could
not keep the covenant. God fulfilled His universal redemptive task through one faithful Israelite-Jesus! This
same tension between the individual and corporate can be seen in that Isa. 49:6 is quoted in Luke 2:32 to refer to
Jesus' ministry and in Acts 13:46-49 referring to the ministry of Paul and Barnabas.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "From the body of My mother" The word "body" is literally "inward parts" (BDB 588). This
speaks of the creation and development of a baby (cf. Ps. 139:13). This same word is used in Isa. 48:19 for
"offspring" (also note Gen. 15:4).

▣ "He named Me" The Servant is called and named before birth by YHWH. He is His
special representative.

This parallels what YHWH did for national Israel in Isa. 43:1. There is a real and continuing
fluidity between the corporate and individual imagery related to the Servant!

verses.zh: 他使我的口如快刀，将我藏在他手荫之下；又使我成为磨亮的箭，将我藏在他箭袋之中；
verses.en: He made my mouth like a sharp sword,he hid me in the hollow of his hand;he made me like a sharpened[NOTE:1] arrow,he hid me in his quiver.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “polished” (so KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); NASB “a select arrow.”

The figurative language emphasizes the servant’s importance as the Lord’s effective instrument. The servant’s mouth, which stands metonymically for his words, is compared to a sharp sword because he will be an effective spokesman on God’s behalf (see 50:4). The Lord holds his hand on the servant, ready to draw and use him at the appropriate time. The servant is like a sharpened arrow reserved in a quiver for just the right moment.
verses.commentary:
49:2 "He has made My mouth like a sharp sword" This is imagery describing a powerful
speaker, and here and in Eph. 6:17; Heb. 4:12 it speaks of divine revelation. It is used to describe the glorified
Christ as Judge in Isa. 11:4; Rev. 1:16; 2:12-16; 19:15,21.

▣ "In the shadow of His hand" This verse has two images of protection and concealment
(cf. Isa. 51:16) until the right time. The Servant's task is specialized and specific. This thought is captured
by the recurrent NT phrase "in the fullness of time" (cf. Mark 1:15; Gal. 4:4; Eph. 1:10; 1 Tim. 2:6; Titus 1:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW, SHADE

verses.zh: 对我说：你是我的仆人以色列；我必因你得荣耀。
verses.en: He said to me, “You are my servant,Israel, through whom I will reveal my splendor.”[NOTE:1]
notes: This verse identifies the servant as Israel. This seems to refer to the exiled nation (cf. 41:8-9; 44:1-2, 21; 45:4; 48:20), but in vv. 5-6 this servant says he has been commissioned to reconcile Israel to God, so he must be distinct from the exiled nation. This servant is an ideal “Israel” who, like Moses of old, mediates a covenant for the nation (see v. 8), leads them out of bondage (v. 9a), and carries out God’s original plan for Israel by positively impacting the pagan nations (see v. 6b). By living according to God’s law, Israel was to be a model of God’s standards of justice to the surrounding nations (Deut 4:6-8). The sinful nation failed, but the servant, the ideal “Israel,” will succeed by establishing justice throughout the earth.
verses.commentary:
49:3-4 The focus of these verses is that the Servant is corporate Israel, but the corporate Servant
has failed its assigned task! Israel was to be YHWH's chosen instrument of world redemption, Isa. 49:6c,d, but
now she herself must be redeemed (cf. Isa. 49:5-6a,b; 53:8d). Verses 5-6 speak of an individual Israelite sent
by YHWH to accomplish His redemptive task.

49:3 "My glory" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod)

verses.zh: 我却说：我劳碌是徒然；我尽力是虚无虚空。然而，我当得的理必在耶和华那里；我的赏赐必在我　神那里。
verses.en: But I thought,[NOTE:1] “I have worked in vain;I have expended my energy for absolutely nothing.”[NOTE:2] But the Lord will vindicate me;my God will reward me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “said” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “I replied.”
Heb “for nothing and emptiness.” Synonyms are combined to emphasize the common idea.
Heb “But my justice is with the Lord, and my reward [or “wage”] with my God.”
verses.commentary:
49:4 There is a contextual question if these verses relate to the failure of Israel or the suffering of
the Messiah. All the VERBS are PERFECT. The ambiguity may be purposeful!

The closing two lines of Isa. 49:4 express an ultimate trust in God's justice and reward
(cf. Isa. 49:5c).

▣ "My reward with My God" I think this links up with Isa. 53:10-11. The reward will be
redemption on a global scale!

verses.zh: 耶和华从我出胎，造就我作他的仆人，要使雅各归向他，使以色列到他那里聚集。原来耶和华看我为尊贵；我的　神也成为我的力量。
verses.en: So now the Lord says,the one who formed me from birth[NOTE:1] to be his servant—he did this[NOTE:2] to restore Jacob to himself,so that Israel might be gathered to him;and I will be honored[NOTE:3] in the Lord’s sight,for my God is my source of strength[NOTE:4]—
notes: Heb “from the womb” (so KJV, NASB).
The words “he did this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text the infinitive construct of purpose is subordinated to the previous statement.
The vav (ו) + imperfect is translated here as a result clause; one might interpret it as indicating purpose, “and so I might be honored.”
Heb “and my God is [perhaps, “having been”] my strength.” The disjunctive structure (vav [ו] + subject + verb) is interpreted here as indicating a causal circumstantial clause.
verses.commentary:
49:5 "To bring Jacob back to Him" This verse and Isa. 49:6b show that the Servant must restore Israel,
therefore, the Servant cannot be Israel (see LXX of Isa. 52:14)

▣ "(For I am honored in the sight of the Lord,

And My God is My strength)

This is a comment from the Servant. It may be a way of encouraging the Servant
amidst the disappointments and opposition He will encounter during His ministry (cf. Isa. 53:1-12).

verses.zh: 现在他说：你作我的仆人，使雅各众支派复兴，使以色列中得保全的归回尚为小事，我还要使你作外邦人的光，叫你施行我的救恩，直到地极。
verses.en: he says, “Is it too insignificant a task for you to be my servant,to reestablish the tribes of Jacob,and restore the remnant[NOTE:1] of Israel?[NOTE:2] I will make you a light to the nations,[NOTE:3] so you can bring[NOTE:4] my deliverance to the remote regions of the earth.”
notes: Heb “the protected [or “preserved”] ones.”
The question is purely rhetorical; it does not imply that the servant was dissatisfied with his commission or that he minimized the restoration of Israel.
See the note at 42:6.
Heb “be” (so KJV, ASV); CEV “you must take.”
verses.commentary:
49:6 "to restore the preserved ones of Israel" This phrase refers to the faithful remnant of the
Chosen People, the chosen instrument of revelation. The hope of a restored, believing Israel is seen in
Zech. 12:10 and Romans 9-11 (see the free commentaries on these books at
www.freebiblecommentary.org).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "I will also make You a light of the nations

So that My salvation may reach to the end of the earth"

Notice the Servant/Messiah had two purposes. If Isa. 49:5 reflects the Israel-focused
ministry of the Gospels, then Isa. 49:6 represents the worldwide expansion of the early church. This
universal spread of the gospel is an oft-repeated theme in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12;
45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1,3; 66:23; Acts 13:46-49). Oh what great news for humanity (cf. Gen. 3:15)!

verses.zh: 救赎主―以色列的圣者耶和华对那被人所藐视、本国所憎恶、官长所虐待的如此说：君王要看见就站起，首领也要下拜；都因信实的耶和华，就是拣选你―以色列的圣者。
verses.en: This is what the Lord,the Protector[NOTE:1] of Israel, their Holy One,[NOTE:2] saysto the one who is despised[NOTE:3] and rejected[NOTE:4] by nations,[NOTE:5] a servant of rulers:“Kings will see and rise in respect,[NOTE:6] princes will bow down,because of the faithful Lord,the Holy One of Israel who has chosen you.”
notes: Heb “redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

The Hebrew text reads literally “to [one who] despises life.” It is preferable to read with the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa לבזוי, which should be vocalized as a passive participle, לִבְזוּי (livzuy, “to the one despised with respect to life” [נֶפֶשׁ is a genitive of specification]). The consonantal sequence וי was probably misread as ה in the MT tradition. The contextual argument favors the 1QIsaa reading. As J. N. Oswalt (Isaiah [NICOT], 2:294) points out, the three terse phrases “convey a picture of lowliness, worthlessness, and helplessness.”
MT’s Piel participle (“to the one who rejects”) does not fit contextually. The form should be revocalized as a Pual, “to the one rejected.”
Parallelism (see “rulers,” “kings,” “princes”) suggests that the singular גּוֹי (goy) be emended to a plural or understood in a collective sense (see 55:5).
For this sense of קוּם (qum), see Gen 19:1; 23:7; 33:10; Lev 19:32; 1 Sam 20:41; 25:41; 1 Kgs 2:19; Job 29:8.
verses.commentary:
49:7 "the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, and its Holy One" This
series of titles (see note at Isa. 48:17) shows us the tension between

- the transcendent and immanent God

- God as Savior and God as Judge

- God as friend and God as boss

We must hold together justification and sanctification. They form one purpose! YHWH
wants a people who display His character.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

▣ "To the despised One,

To the One abhorred by the nation,

To the Servant of rulers"

This implies the lowliness of the Servant, even the rejection of the Servant (cf. Isa. 50:4-11;
52:14-53:6; Psalm 22). The MT has the SINGULAR "nation," but used in a collective sense.
It is parallel to "rulers," "Kings," and "princes." But ultimately all earthly authority will acknowledge Him (cf. Phil. 2:6-11, which
alludes to Isa. 45:22-23). Matthew 12:18-21; Acts 8:26-35; and 1 Pet. 2:21-25 quote Isaiah as referring to Jesus.

Is it not ironical that the one despised and abhorred by the nations (cf. Psalm 2) is
the very one that will bring salvation to the nations!

▣ "Kings shall see and arise,

Princes shall also bow down" These are VERBS of homage.

- arise ‒ BDB 877, KB 1056, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Gen. 19:1;
23:7; Exod. 33:10; 1 Sam. 20:41

- bow down ‒ BDB 1105, KB 295, Hishtaphel IMPERFECT, cf. Gen. 19:1;
23:7; Exod. 33:10; Lev. 19:32; 1 Sam. 20:4

The One despised and abhorred has now, by YHWH's help, become the respected, honored One!

▣ "Because of the Lord who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel
who has chosen You" Here is the key to our hope, YHWH's faithfulness. Our hope is in the character
of the One who calls, promises, and redeems!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：在悦纳的时候，我应允了你；在拯救的日子，我济助了你。我要保护你，使你作众民的中保（中保：原文是约）；复兴遍地，使人承受荒凉之地为业。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says:“At the time I decide to show my favor, I will respond to you;in the day of deliverance I will help you;I will protect you[NOTE:1] and make you a covenant mediator for people,[NOTE:2] to rebuild[NOTE:3] the land[NOTE:4] and to reassign the desolate property.
notes: The translation assumes the verb is derived from the root נָצָר (natsar, “protect”). Some prefer to derive it from the root יָצָר (yatsar, “form”).

Heb “a covenant of people.” A person cannot literally be a covenant; בְּרִית (berit) is probably metonymic here, indicating a covenant mediator. Here עָם (ʿam, “people”) appears to refer to Israel. See the note at 42:6.
The Hiphil of קוּם (qum, “arise”) is probably used here in the sense of “rebuild.”
The “land” probably stands by metonymy for the ruins within it.
verses.commentary:
49:8 Notice that "in a favorable time" and "in a day of salvation" are parallel. This text is
quoted in 2 Cor. 6:2. It is used in Ps. 69:13-15 for a day of deliverance. It can denote physical or
spiritual deliverance/salvation (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION [OT]).
The Year of Jubilee (Lev. 25:10) symbolized this radical forgiveness
of debts. In this context they are talking about the return to Palestine, which began with Cyrus'
decree in 538 B.C. and was accomplished in several waves.

- Sheshbazzar ‒ Ezra 1

- Zerubbabel and Joshua ‒ Ezra 2

- Nehemiah ‒ Nehemiah 1

- Ezra ‒ Nehemiah 8

Notice the VERBS in Isa. 49:8 that describe YHWH's actions.

- I have answered You ‒ Qal PERFECT (BDB 772, KB 851)

- I have helped You ‒ Qal PERFECT (BDB 740, KB 810)

- I will keep You ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 665, KB 718, "watch," "guard," "keep")

- I will give You ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 678, KB 733)

- to restore the land ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 877, KB 1086)

- to make them inherit ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB635, KB 686)

These personal redemptive actions of YHWH are also highlighted in Ezek. 36:21-36.

▣

NASB
"give You for a covenant of the people"

NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"give You as a covenant to the people"

TEV
"through you make a covenant with all peoples"

JPSOA
"appoionted you a covenant people"

REB
"destined you to be a light for peoples"

LXX
"given you for a covenant of the nations"

NJB
"have appointed you to be the covenant for a people"

NET
"and make you a covenant mediator for people"

This phrase was used earlier in Isa. 42:6 in which
the themes of Isa. 49:6,8 coincide. YHWH's covenant with Abraham and his seed had a wider orientation
than just Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S
ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). It was also for the whole world (i.e. the nations; see the different translations of
this line of poetry). This is the logical and theological
implication of monotheism-only one God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM), all humans created in God's image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27), and a promise to redeem
all humans in Gen. 3:15, long before there was a nation of Israel.

49:8d-12 These verses are imagery of sheep feeding in abundant pastures. They reflect the
covenant blessing of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-28. God's people have been restored to the Promised Land! Paul
uses this text for the New Age in 2 Cor. 6:2. Verse 10 is also used in Rev. 7:16, which shows Gentiles are included.

verses.zh: 对那被捆绑的人说：出来吧！对那在黑暗的人说：显露吧！他们在路上必得饮食，在一切净光的高处必有食物。
verses.en: You will say[NOTE:1] to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’and to those who are in dark dungeons,[NOTE:2] ‘Emerge.’[NOTE:3] They will graze beside the roads;on all the slopes they will find pasture.
notes: Heb “to say.” In the Hebrew text the infinitive construct is subordinated to what precedes.
Heb “in darkness” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “the prisoners of darkness.”
Heb “show yourselves” (so ASV, NAB, NASB).
verses.commentary:
49:9 The Israelites are described as being in prison (i.e. prisoners, BDB 63, cf. Isa. 42:7; 61:1).

- to those who are bound

- to those who are in darkness

They are told to

- go forth ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 422, KB 425)

- show yourselves ‒ Niphal IMPERATIVE (lit. "uncover yourself," BDB162, KB 191)

verses.zh: 不饥不渴，炎热和烈日必不伤害他们；因为怜恤他们的必引导他们，领他们到水泉旁边。
verses.en: They will not be hungry or thirsty;the sun’s oppressive heat will not beat down on them,[NOTE:1] for one who has compassion on them will guide them;he will lead them to springs of water.
notes: Heb “and the heat and the sun will not strike them.” In Isa 35:7, its only other occurrence in the OT, שָׁרָב (sharav) stands parallel to “parched ground” and in contrast to “pool.” In later Hebrew and Aramaic it refers to “dry heat, heat of the sun” (Jastrow 1627 s.v.). Here it likely has this nuance and forms a hendiadys with “sun.”
verses.commentary:
49:10 "He who has compassion on them will lead them" These are descriptive titles for YHWH.

- the one who has compassion ‒ Piel PARTICIPLE (BDB 933, KB 1216)

- the one who leads them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 624, KB 675)

- the one who will guide them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 624, KB 675)

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

▣ The agricultural imagery of provision is from Isa. 49:9 continue.

- no hunger

- no thirst

- no heat stroke (used only here and Isa. 35:7)

The return home will be easy, protected and with abundant provisions (i.e. new Exodus and Wildeness
Wandering Period). This same imagery is used in Rev. 7:16 of the Messianic period. YHWH's Messiah is
their shepherd (cf. Ps. 121:5-6).

verses.zh: 我必使我的众山成为大道；我的大路也被修高。
verses.en: I will make all my mountains into a road;I will construct my roadways.”
verses.commentary:
49:11 Access to Jerusalem is metaphorically assured by the removal of all obstacles and the
provision of a repaired, even raised, roadway (cf. Isa. 11:16; 19:23; 35:8; 62:10).

There will be a free-flowing movement between nations for the purpose of worshiping
YHWH. The nations have come!

It is interesting how many times Isaiah uses the imagery of a highway.

- a highway for the exiled Jews to return, Isa. 11:16; 57:14

- a highway for Gentile worshipers to come, Isa. 19:23

- a highway of holiness, Isa. 26:7; 35:8; 43:19; 49:11; 51:10

- a Messianic highway, Isa. 40:3; 42:16

verses.zh: 看哪，这些从远方来；这些从北方、从西方来；这些从秦（原文是希尼）国来。
verses.en: Look, they come from far away!Look, some come from the north and west,and others from the land of Sinim.[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT reads “Sinim” here; the Dead Sea Scrolls read “Syene,” a location in Egypt associated with modern Aswan. A number of recent translations adopt this reading: “Syene” (NAB, NRSV); “Aswan” (NIV); “Egypt” (NLT).sn The precise location of the land of Sinim is uncertain, but since the north and west are mentioned in the previous line, it was a probably located in the distant east or south.
verses.commentary:
49:12 ". . .And these from the land of Sinim" The exact location is uncertain. The thrust
of the text is that God will bring all His people home, even from the farthest land. Notice the variety
in the following translations.

- MT, NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta ‒ "Sinim"

- NRSV, REB ‒ "Syene" (BDB 696, cf. Ezek. 30:6)

- TEV, NIV, NJB ‒ "Aswan"

- DSS of Isaiah ‒ "Syenians"

- LXX ‒ "Syenians"

All of these are various spellings (except the LXX) of the ancient and modern city in
southern Egypt which had a large Jewish population (cf. Ezek. 30:6, #2), also known in Greek literature as Elephantine.
Today its name is Aswan.

verses.zh: 诸天哪，应当欢呼！大地啊，应当快乐！众山哪，应当发声歌唱！因为耶和华已经安慰他的百姓，也要怜恤他困苦之民。
verses.en: Shout for joy, O sky![NOTE:1] Rejoice, O earth!Let the mountains give a joyful shout!For the Lord consoles his peopleand shows compassion to the[NOTE:2] oppressed.
notes: Or “O heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “his” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
49:13 "O heaven. . .O earth. . .O mountains" These have served as witnesses to YHWH's
judgment against His people (Isaiah 48). Now they serve as joyful witnesses of God's faithfulness
(cf. Isa. 44:23)!

Notice the series of IMPERATIVES.

- shout ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 943, KB 1247)

- rejoice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 189)

- break forth ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 822, KB 953)

▣ "comforted" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

verses.zh: 锡安说：耶和华离弃了我；主忘记了我。
verses.en: “Zion said, ‘The Lord has abandoned me,the Lord[NOTE:1] has forgotten me.’
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
verses.commentary:
49:14-21 These verses are words of encouragement by YHWH to a discouraged and barren
Jerusalem (i.e. Zion). Notice the number of times the word "forget' (BDB 1013, KB 1489) is used.

- "the Lord has forgotten me" ‒ Qal PERFECT

- "can a woman forget her nursing child" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

- "even these may forget" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

- "I will not forget you" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

YHWH uses anthropomorphic language to describe His love and faithful protection
to the returnees by means of a feminine imagery (hear sermon online at
www.freebiblecommentary.org under
"Difficult and Controversial Texts," number 111, "The Femininity of God."

verses.zh: 妇人焉能忘记她吃奶的婴孩，不怜恤她所生的儿子？即或有忘记的，我却不忘记你。
verses.en: Can a woman forget her baby who nurses at her breast?[NOTE:1] Can she withhold compassion from the child she has borne?[NOTE:2] Even if mothers[NOTE:3] were to forget,I could never forget you![NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “her suckling”; NASB “her nursing child.”
Heb “so as not to have compassion on the son of her womb?”
Heb “these” (so ASV, NASB).

The argument of v. 15 seems to develop as follows: The Lord has an innate attachment to Zion, just like a mother does for her infant child. But even if mothers were to suddenly abandon their children, the Lord would never forsake Zion. In other words, the Lord’s attachment to Zion is like a mother’s attachment to her infant child, but even stronger.
verses.commentary:
49:15 This is powerful imagery of YHWH's covenant love (cf. Isa. 66:9-13). YHWH is described
in terms of a nursing mother.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

verses.zh: 看哪，我将你铭刻在我掌上；你的墙垣常在我眼前。
verses.en: Look, I have inscribed your name[NOTE:1] on my palms;your walls are constantly before me.
notes: Heb “you.” Here the pronoun is put by metonymy for the person’s name.
verses.commentary:
49:16-17 This is more powerful imagery of YHWH's constant remembrance of His covenant
with Abraham's descendants. Even when Jerusalem is in ruins, YHWH's people envision the new day
of restoration (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

49:16a This may reflect Isa. 44:5. The covenant people, Abraham's descendants, are always on
YHWH's mind and heart. This is also true of the city of Jerusalem (v. 16b).

verses.zh: 你的儿女必急速归回；毁坏你的，使你荒废的，必都离你出去，
verses.en: Your children hurry back,while those who destroyed and devastated you depart.
verses.commentary:
49:17

NASB
"Your builders hurry"

NKJV
"your sons make haste"

NJB
"your rebuilders are hurrying"

JPSOA
"swiftly your children are coming"

NET
"Your children hurry back"

The UBS Text Project (p. 134-135) shows the two options.

- your sons, בניך ‒ MT, DSS, Peshitta (cf. Isa. 49:25e)

- your builders, בוניך ‒ which the UBS calls "Babylonian vocalization"

The UBS Text Project, pp. 134-135, gives option #2 a C rating (considerable doubt), p. 134.

The second line is also in question.

- REV ‒ "Your builders outstrip your destroyers"

- NEB ‒ "Those who are to rebuild you make better speed than those who pulled you down"

This difference involves only a revocalization of the Hebrew consonants (UBS Text Project, p. 135).

verses.zh: 你举目向四方观看；他们都聚集来到你这里。耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓：你必要以他们为妆饰佩戴，以他们为华带束腰，像新妇一样。
verses.en: Look all around you![NOTE:1] All of them gather to you.As surely as I live,” says the Lord,“you will certainly wear all of them like jewelry;you will put them on as if you were a bride.
notes: Heb “Lift up around your eyes and see.”
verses.commentary:
49:18 Jerusalem was destroyed! She is personified as a mother without children
(cf. Isa. 49:20-21). Her husband, YHWH, has now restored her and provided numerous
children as the crown of her old age!

YHWH challenges the returnees to

- lift up your eyes ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 669, KB 724)

- look around ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 906, KB 1157)

▣ "As I live, declares the Lord" This is an oath statement with
a play on the Hebrew VERB "to be," which is Israel's God's chosen title (cf. Exod. 3:13-14). YHWH
is the ever-living, only-living One!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "all of them" Tis could refer to

- the childen of the returnees (v. 17)

- the former destroyers who are now rebuilders (v. 17)

verses.zh: 至于你荒废凄凉之处，并你被毁坏之地，现今众民居住必显为太窄；吞灭你的必离你遥远。
verses.en: Yes, your land lies in ruins;it is desolate and devastated.[NOTE:1] But now you will be too small to hold your residents,and those who devoured you will be far away.
notes: Heb “Indeed your ruins and your desolate places, and the land of your destruction.” This statement is abruptly terminated in the Hebrew text and left incomplete.
verses.commentary:
49:19-20 These verses are imagery of the large number of returnees and their children who fill
up the Promsed Land. This reflects God's stated purpose, "be fruitful and multiply," in Genesis 1 and 9.

verses.zh: 你必听见丧子之后所生的儿女说：这地方我居住太窄，求你给我地方居住。
verses.en: Yet the children born during your time of bereavementwill say within your hearing,‘This place is too cramped for us,[NOTE:1] make room for us so we can live here.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “me.” The singular is collective.
Heb “draw near to me so I can dwell.”

verses.zh: 那时你心里必说：我既丧子独居，是被掳的，漂流在外。谁给我生这些？谁将这些养大呢？撇下我一人独居的时候，这些在哪里呢？
verses.en: Then you will think to yourself,[NOTE:1] ‘Who bore these children for me?I was bereaved and barren,dismissed and divorced.[NOTE:2] Who raised these children?Look, I was left all alone;where did these children come from?’”
notes: Heb “and you will say in your heart.”
Or “exiled and thrust away”; NIV “exiled and rejected.”
verses.commentary:
49:21-22 Those who return to Jerusalem, which symbolizes the worship of YHWH
(i.e. the temple), will be so many that the city cannot physically contain them all!

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必向列国举手，向万民竖立大旗；他们必将你的众子怀中抱来，将你的众女肩上扛来。
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says:“Look I will raise my hand to the nations;I will raise my signal flag to the peoples.They will bring your sons in their armsand carry your daughters on their shoulders.
verses.commentary:
49:22-23 In Isa. 49:7 the leaders of the Gentile nations rejected and rebelled against God's
Messiah (cf. Psalm 2). Now they come repentantly to Jerusalem bringing God's covenant people with
them. This verse is not meant to magnify the Old Covenant, but the covenant-making God!
The Gentiles' reverence for YHWH will be seen in their respect for His people (cf. Isa. 45:14).

49:22 "set up My standard to the peoples" This is parallel to "lift up My hand to the nations." The
Servant will be a signal/flag for the nations (i.e. Gentiles) to rally (cf. Isa. 11:10,12). The ultimate goal of
the covenant people's restoration is the restoration of all humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 列王必作你的养父；王后必作你的乳母。他们必将脸伏地，向你下拜，并舔你脚上的尘土。你便知道我是耶和华；等候我的必不致羞愧。
verses.en: Kings will be your children’s[NOTE:1] guardians;their princesses will nurse your children.[NOTE:2] With their faces to the ground they will bow down to you,and they will lick the dirt on[NOTE:3] your feet.Then you will recognize that I am the Lord;those who wait patiently for me are not put to shame.
notes: Heb “your,” but Zion here stands by metonymy for her children (see v. 22b).
Heb “you.” See the preceding note.
Or “at your feet” (NAB, NIV); NLT “from your feet.”
verses.commentary:
49:23 "And you will know that I am the Lord" Israel
was meant to be a witness to the nations. Now the nations will be a witness to Israel. As Gentiles trust in
YHWH and are converted in large numbers, this is a sign to Israel that God is with them but that they must
also have faith (cf. Romans 9-11).

▣ "Those who hopefully wait for Me will not be put to shame" The concept of "wait" is
found often in Isaiah: 25:9; 26:8; 40:31 (Ps. 37:9). This is analogous to those who "trust in" the Servant!
Notice the personal element (i.e. "Me").

The phrase "put to shame" is another theme of the OT (cf. Isa. 45:17; Ps. 25:3; Joel 2:27).
Those who wait/trust will not be shamed/disappointed!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

verses.zh: 勇士抢去的岂能夺回？该掳掠的岂能解救吗？
verses.en: Can spoils be taken from a warrior,or captives be rescued from a conqueror?[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text has צָדִיק (tsadiq, “a righteous [one]”), but this makes no sense in the parallelism. The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa reads correctly עריץ (“violent [one], tyrant”; see v. 25).
verses.commentary:
49:24-26 These verses are imagery for a second exodus experience. God is delivering His
people again from powerful world empires. It is significant that God's purpose in this deliverance, like
His first deliverance, is not only that His covenant people might go free but that all nations will
know Him (cf. Isa. 49:26c; 45:6; Mal. 1:11).

As a Christian, I wonder if this context was in Jesus' mind in Matt. 12:22-29; Luke 11:14-22.
Jesus' exorcisms clearly show His power over evil. The third, and most important, Exodus imagery is Jesus'
defeat of sin and Satan! Often, Jesus' ministry uses Exodus imagery.

49:24b

NASB, NRSV, NJB, TEV
"a tyrant"

NKJV
"the righteous"

REB
"the ruthless"

"victor"

"giants"

The MT translation is followed by NKJV, but the others come from
the DSS, Syriac, and Vulgate.

- righteous ‒ צדיק (BDB 843)

- tyrant ‒ עריץ (BDB 792)

The UBS Text Project, p. 136, gives option #2 a C rating (considerable doubt). However,
#1 makes no sense in this context, unless it is used as an ADJECTIVE for YHWH's
people. See Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, p. 207.

verses.zh: 但耶和华如此说：就是勇士所掳掠的，也可以夺回；强暴人所抢的，也可以解救。与你相争的，我必与他相争；我要拯救你的儿女。
verses.en: Indeed,” says the Lord,“captives will be taken from a warrior;spoils will be rescued from a conqueror.I will oppose your adversaryand I will rescue your children.
verses.commentary:
49:25 "For I will contend" This is "court scene" imagery. Possibly its use in Jer. 50:34
sheds light on this verse.

YHWH/Servant has changed from Prosecutor to Advocate (i.e. legal terminology)!

49:26a-b Israel's enemies (i.e. Assyria, Neo-Babylon) are completely defeated.

- eat their own flesh

- drink their own blood

This imagery refers to the horrors of siege warfare in the ANE.

49:26c "And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior" It is
theologically difficult to know if these Servant Songs refer to the restoration and salvation of national Israel or
to the restoration and salvation of all mankind.

In the immediate context, it must refer to corporate Israel, YHWH's covenant people. But, NT
authors use these verses to describe the ministry of Jesus. So, these are multiple fulfillment prophecies. I have
mentioned how this section of Isaiah (i.e. Isaiah 40-66) often moves between promises to the returning exiles and
promises of a universal Messiah.

Jesus fulfilled the OT (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). He opened the door for all the children of Adam and
Eve to find Him (i.e. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

49:26c-d Notice again the powerful titles for the Deity of Israel (cf. Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 44:6,24;
47:4; 48:17; 49:7,26; 54:5,8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16).

- Your Savior

- Your Redeemer

- the Mighty One of Jacob, cf. Isa. 1:4

verses.zh: 并且我必使那欺压你的吃自己的肉，也要以自己的血喝醉，好像喝甜酒一样。凡有血气的必都知道我―耶和华是你的救主，是你的救赎主，是雅各的大能者。
verses.en: I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh;they will get drunk on their own blood, as if it were wine.[NOTE:1] Then all humankind[NOTE:2] will recognize thatI am the Lord, your Deliverer, your Protector,[NOTE:3] the Powerful One of Jacob.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Verse 26a depicts siege warfare and bloody defeat. The besieged enemy will be so starved they will eat their own flesh. The bloodstained bodies lying on the blood-soaked battle site will look as if they collapsed in drunkenness.
Heb “flesh” (so KJV, NASB).
Heb “your redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.
Or “the Mighty One of Jacob.” See 1:24.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The literary unit of Isaiah 40-66 focuses on God's restoration of His people through the
work of "His Servant" (esp. Isa. 49-57).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

- This passage is known as the second Servant Song. See full list of the Songs/Poems
at the Introduction to Isa. 42, A.

- This chapter has several important truths.

- YHWH has prepared a special Savior/Servant

- This special Servant will bring all people to Him

- YHWH has not forgotten His Servant nation, Israel

Who is this Servant?

- obviously some contests must refer to Israel/Judah (cf. v. 3a)

- some contexts, such as Isa. 52:13-53:12 refer to the ideal Israelite, the Messiah

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

- Isaiah himself and his own mission (v. 4)

- a faithful remnant of Israel; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

- The NT uses several texts from Isaiah and applies them to Jesus (i.e. Matt. 12:18-21; Acts 8:21-35; 1 Pet. 2:21-25).

Remember, there is a fluidity in Isaiah 40-66 between the corporate and the individual.

- Note the parallel themes and imagery between Isa. 40 and 49.
